nodes.label: Phase 1 Platform Governance
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 is documentation-only so implementation, dependency installation, migrations, endpoints, UI, and the Forge bridge remain blocked until Phase 2 is explicitly authorized.

nodes.label: Dedicated Server Promotion Gate
nodes.rationale: Raw runtime files cannot be promoted until client compatibility, provenance and licensing, secret removal, side classification, and clean-environment boot and connection are verified.

nodes.label: Project-Owned Source Publication Gate
nodes.rationale: Local patches, stubs, tools, and compatibility sources remain evidence until authorship and licensing are reviewed.

nodes.label: Evidence and Release Documentation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Documentation records decisions and evidence while publishable client and server sources stay separate and uncertified.

nodes.label: ADR-001 TypeScript Control Plane and Java Forge Bridge
nodes.rationale: Shared contracts favor strict TypeScript for web and services, while Java 17 is confined to Forge-loaded code to avoid an unsuitable language boundary and reduce privileged Java surface.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001 typescript control plane and java forge bridge

nodes.label: ADR-002 Outbound Authenticated Server Agent
nodes.rationale: An instance-identified agent initiates mutually authenticated outbound communication so the Minecraft host exposes no broad administrative port and central intent stays separate from local execution.

nodes.label: ADR-003 Signed Immutable Release Manifest
nodes.rationale: Versioned signed manifests, immutable SHA-256 artifacts, and atomic channel pointers enable integrity, incremental updates, cache, rollback, and launcher independence.

nodes.label: ADR-004 PostgreSQL Durable Job Queue
nodes.rationale: A PostgreSQL lease and row-lock queue keeps jobs, authorization, idempotency, and audit in one transaction while avoiding premature broker infrastructure at initial scale.

nodes.label: ADR-005 Reviewed Canonical Client Catalog
nodes.rationale: A reviewed catalog replaces unsafe runtime copying with an auditable, reproducible, launcher-independent source; unknown provenance, side, license, or dependencies block stable publication.
